title: Simple, Affordable, and Modular Patterning of Cells using DNA
protocol: Design experiment considering feature size, feature spacing, number of cell types involved, and arrangement of cells with respect to one another.
Refer to Supplemental File 1 for a guide on experimental design.
Use computer-aided design software to draw a rectangle of the dimensions of a standard microscope slide (25 mm x 75 mm).
Draw four rectangular regions that are 10 mm wide and 10 mm long, distributed evenly across the slide.
Within each region, draw features of the desired size, shape, and spacing for the experiment.
Create versions of master drawings corresponding to each cell type when patterning multiple cell types.
Order a high-resolution transparency photomask with features drawn in transparent and larger regions black.
Fabricate fiducial markers on aldehyde-functionalized slides before DNA patterning if patterning multiple cell types.
Apply S1813 positive photoresist as described in steps 2.3 - 2.11.
Deposit a thin film (100 Angstroms) of titanium onto the slide using electron-gun evaporation.
Remove excess metal and photoresist using acetone.
Prepare a 20 µM solution of a 5'-amine-modified oligo in DNA buffer.
Pre-heat a hot plate to 100 °C.
Attach an aldehyde-functionalized glass slide to the rotor of a spin coater using double-sided tape or vacuum.
Label a corner of the slide by scratching the glass with a diamond scribe.
Use a disposable pipette to drop positive photoresist onto an aldehyde slide.
Add small drops of photoresist across the slide for even coating.
Spin the slide at 3000 rpm for 30 seconds using a spin coater.
Place the slide on a hotplate at 100 °C for 1.5 minutes (soft bake).
Remove the slide from the hotplate.
Position a photomask with desired features onto the slide and secure it with glass.
Cover the setup in an opaque box.
Expose the slide to UV light (365 nm, 360 mW, 5 inches from slide, total radiant energy density 100 mJ/cm²) for 2 minutes.
Immerse the slide in developer solution for 3-5 minutes.
Rinse excess developer solution with water.
Dry the slide under a stream of air or nitrogen.
Confirm photolithography success by examining the slide under a microscope.
Store the slide in the dark while preparing other slides.
Add a droplet of the 20 µM amine-modified oligo solution onto each photopatterned region of the slide.
Gently spread the droplet across the entire region using a pipette tip without scratching the slide.
Bake the slide in a 65-70 °C oven until the DNA solution has fully dried onto the slide surface (about 1 h).
Weigh out 100 mg of sodium borohydride.
Add 40 mL of phosphate-buffered saline to the sodium borohydride, gently mix.
Place patterned, baked slides in a 15 cm cell-culture dish.
Transfer the mixture containing PBS and sodium borohydride into the dish with the patterned slides.
Let the reaction proceed for 15 min with gentle shaking.
Perform the reductive amination step in a fume hood.
Keep sodium borohydride solution waste in an open or loosely capped container in the fume hood for at least 24 h.
Wash unreacted DNA twice with 0.1% sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS) in water.
Wash the slide three times with distilled water.
Dry the slide under a stream of nitrogen or air.
Rinse the slide with acetone to remove remaining photoresist.
Make slide hydrophobic (optional).
Rinse slide with 10% acetic acid.
Dry slide under an air stream.
Prepare a solution of 60 mL methylene chloride, 0.6 mL triethylamine, and 0.6 mL (tridecafluoro-1,1,2,2-tetrahydrooctyl) dimethylchlorosilane in a glass Coplin jar.
Stir the solution with a metal spatula to mix thoroughly.
Add the slide to the silane solution in the Coplin jar.
Place the Coplin jar on an orbital shaker set to 60-80 rpm.
Allow the reaction to proceed for 15 minutes.
Use metal forceps to remove the slide from the silane solution.
Immerse the slide in a Coplin jar containing methylene chloride for 1 minute.
Agitate the slide in a 50 mL conical tube containing ethanol.
Agitate the slide in a 50 mL conical tube containing distilled water.
Inspect the slide after removing it from the water.
Allow the slides to dry fully and store them in a vacuum desiccator until use.
Remove the wafer from the hotplate.
Place the photomask (emulsion side down) on top of the wafer and weigh it down with a glass disc to ensure contact between the photomask and the slide.
Expose the wafer with UV light at 365 nm for a radiant energy density of 350 mJ/cm².
Bake the wafer on the hotplate for 12-15 minutes.
Place the wafer in a wide glass container.
Cover the wafer with SU-8 developer solution.
Shake and agitate the wafer in the developer solution for at least 15 minutes.
Use forceps to remove the wafer from the developer solution.
Rinse the wafer for 5 seconds by spraying more developer solution from a squirt bottle.
Spray the wafer with isopropyl alcohol to rinse.
If a white precipitate appears, return the wafer to the developer solution and develop for longer.
Dry the wafer under a stream of air or nitrogen.
Bake the slide for 5 minutes.
Add polydimethylsiloxane elastomer and crosslinker in a 10:1 ratio (by mass) in a weigh boat.
Stir vigorously to ensure even mixing.
De-gas the PDMS in a vacuum desiccator for 15-30 minutes until no more bubbles are visible.
Place the master wafer in a 15 cm tissue culture dish.
Pour PDMS over the wafer.
If bubbles appear, de-gas in a vacuum desiccator for a few minutes.
Bake the PDMS in a 60 °C oven for 3 hours.
Cut out PDMS flow cells from the master wafer.
Plasma oxidize the cut-out PDMS with room air for 90 seconds.
Create an inlet and outlet by cutting open the top and bottom of each flow cell, leaving 1-2 mm of PDMS on each side.
Place the PDMS flow cells on the patterned slide in the location of each patterned region as indicated by the photomask.
Add 50 µL of PBS + 1% BSA to the inlet of each flow cell.
Confirm that the flow cell is completely filled with PBS + 1% BSA and check for large bubbles.
Prepare cholesterol-modified DNA solutions by mixing 3 µL of a 100 µM stock solution of Universal Anchor Strand with 3 µL of a 100 µM stock solution of Adapter Strand.
Incubate the mixed oligos for one minute to pre-hybridize them.
Add 69 µL of PBS to create a 4 µM Universal Anchor + Adapter solution.
Add 3 µL of a 100 µM Universal cholesterol-modified Co-Anchor Strand stock solution to 12 µL of PBS.
Create a 20 µM solution.
Prepare a single-cell suspension for each set of cells in the experiment.
For adherent cells, use trypsin or other dissociation agent to remove the cells from the culture flask.
Add culture media to neutralize the trypsin and centrifuge to pellet the cells.
For non-adherent cells, collect the cell suspension and centrifuge to pellet the cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 1 mL of ice-cold PBS or serum-free media.
Transfer 1-3 million cells to a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge at 160 x g for 4 min.
If the cell type is prone to clumping/aggregation, use PBS without calcium and magnesium ions for all wash steps to reduce unwanted cell aggregation.
If viability is a particular concern, use serum-free media instead of PBS.
Media containing fetal bovine serum is not recommended for cell labeling as it can hinder incorporation of lipid-modified oligos.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 75 µL of ice-cold PBS or serum-free media.
Keep the cells in an ice bucket throughout the labeling and washing process to maximize cell viability and minimize loss of the cholesterol-modified oligos from the cell surface.
Add 75 µL of the 4 µM Universal Anchor + Adapter solution to the microcentrifuge tube containing the cell suspension.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 min on ice.
Add 15 µL of the Universal Co-Anchor Solution to the microcentrifuge tube.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting.
Incubate for 5 min on ice.
Remove excess oligos from the cell suspension.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold PBS or serum-free media to the microcentrifuge tube.
Mix with a P1000 pipette.
Centrifuge at 160 x g for 4 min at 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant.
Repeat two more times.
Resuspend the cells in ice-cold PBS or serum-free media to create a cell-dense solution of at least 25 million cells/mL.
Pick up slide and tilt it slightly.
Add 25 µl of cell suspension to the inlet of each flow cell on the patterned slide.
Remove PBS + 1% BSA solution from the outlet, allowing the cell suspension to fill the PDMS flow cell.
Incubate on ice or at room temperature for 30 s.
Aspirate 5 μl of cell suspension from the outlet of the slide and add it back into the inlet.
Repeat this process 10 times per flow cell.
Gently pipette PBS or serum-free media into the inlet of each flow cell to wash out excess cells.
Collect the cell suspension from the outlet.
Repeat washing steps 2-4 times or until a visual inspection under the microscope confirms no excess cells remaining.
Save excess cells from the first wash if patterning efficiency is unsatisfactory.
Centrifuge and resuspend excess cells in a lower volume of PBS for higher cell density.
Repeat steps involving cell washing, centrifuging, and resuspending as necessary.
Start with the least abundant cell type when multiple types are patterned directly on surface templates.
Avoid pooling cells from different rounds to maintain patterning efficiency.
Add media to Petri dish containing slide after final round of cellular assembly if cells remain on glass.
Gently use forceps to nudge PDMS flow cells off the slide after adding media.
Prepare hydrogel precursor solution containing 2% DNase for 3D culture (optional).
Transfer cells into prepared hydrogel for embedding and subsequent 3D culture.
Add 50 µL of hydrogel solution containing 2% DNase to the inlet of each flow cell.
Aspirate excess fluid from the outlet, driving the hydrogel solution into the flow cell.
For viscous hydrogel precursors, tilt the slide slightly to help the hydrogel flow into the flow cell.
Incubate the slide at 37 °C for 30-45 min to allow the hydrogel to set and cleave DNA-based adhesion between cells and surface.
Remove each flow cell from the slide and place on top of hydrogel precursor solution.
Add 50 µL of hydrogel precursor to a well of a 2-well chamber slide or a 6-well plate.
Pipette 10 µL of PBS on either side of each flow cell.
Use a razor blade or fine-point tweezers to distribute the PBS along the full length of the flow cell.
Gently lift the sides of the flow cell so that the PBS rushes underneath the hydrogel.
Use a razor blade to gently move the flow cell to the edge of the glass slide.
Invert the slide and nudge the flow cell off the slide using a razor blade.
Pick up the flow cell with curved forceps and invert it so that the cells are on the bottom.
Place the inverted flow cell on top of the droplet of hydrogel precursor solution.
Incubate for at least 30 minutes so that the hydrogel containing the patterned cells can bind to the hydrogel underlay, resulting in full embedding of the patterned cells.
Remove the PDMS flow cell using curved forceps oriented along the long axis of the flow cell and gently nudge until it pops off and floats into the media.
Add enough media to immerse the PDMS flow cell.
Spread the curved forceps and apply gentle pressure to the walls of the PDMS flow cell.
Apply force in the direction of the long axis of the flow cell.
Order a fluorescently modified (FAM or AF647) oligonucleotide complementary to the surface adhesion sequence of the Adapter Strand being used.
Label cells with CMO DNA and wash out excess DNA as described in Step 5.
Resuspend labeled cells in 200 µL of ice-cold PBS.
Make up a 4 µM solution of the fluorescently labeled complementary oligonucleotide in PBS.
Add 200 µL of the fluorescently labeled oligonucleotide solution to the cell suspension.
Incubate on ice for 5 minutes.
Add 1 mL of ice-cold PBS and mix thoroughly.
Centrifuge the cells to pellet them.
Remove the supernatant.
Repeat this process two more times to wash out any DNA that has not hybridized.
Perform analytical flow cytometry to quantify the presence of DNA on the cell surface.
On a flow cytometer, analyze control cells that have not been labeled with DNA.
Set up gates based on this population.
Analyze CMO-labeled cells that have been treated with a fluorescently labeled complementary oligonucleotide.
Calculate mean fluorescence intensity.
